mainTopic: Does reaping the עומר override שבת for רבי, and which מנחות have a קומץ removed with the leftovers going to the כהנים?
overview: The גמרא continues asking whether reaping the עומר overrides שבת, and what that says about an עומר reaped at the wrong time. It explains that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון knew his father's teaching but limited it, because in the fats-and-limbs case the שחיטה had already overridden שבת. רבי, who holds that a wrongly-timed עומר is valid, must then hold that reaping the עומר does not override שבת at all. The גמרא defends this against several משניות by saying they do not follow רבי. It also reads one משנה of רבי's as talking about offering the עומר, not reaping it. A ברייתא of רבי about the מועדים seems to show that reaping does override שבת. The גמרא answers that the עומר overrides שבת for its offering, and the שתי הלחם for their baking, because רבי holds תנור מקדש. A challenge to that idea is answered by רב נחמן בר יצחק: 'holy' in רבי's ברייתא means 'fixed'. Then פרק רבי ישמעאל ends, and a new משנה lists the מנחות that have a קומץ removed. The גמרא discusses רב פפא's rule of ten and looks for the source that the כהנים eat the leftovers of barley מנחות. חזקיה's source from a פסוק is challenged at the end of the amud, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Didn't the son know his father's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון could ignore his own father's teaching that a מצוה at its proper time is precious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון not hear this teaching?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He must have known his father's teaching, so how can he prove from the fact that reaping overrides שבת that a wrongly-timed עומר is invalid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון taught that a מצוה done at its right time is so precious that it may override שבת even when it would still be valid later. If so, the fact that reaping the עומר overrides שבת proves nothing about whether a late reaping is invalid. The son surely heard his father's teaching, so the proof seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: son of רבי...
he did not hear it (did he not know this?)
heard / known

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon
did he not hear this?!
phrases.notes: "This" is his father's teaching that a מצוה at its proper time is precious, which the גמרא just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion: it applies רבי שמעון's teaching against his son's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view that an עומר reaped not at its proper time is invalid, as proven from reaping overriding שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His father's principle of מצוה בשעתה explains why reaping overrides שבת without making a late reaping invalid. So the son should not be able to use that proof.

steps.title: The fats-and-limbs case is different because the slaughter already overrode שבת
steps.stepSummary: He knew his father's teaching but limits it: burning fats on שבת is allowed only because the שחיטה already overrode שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is different there, because the slaughtering already overrode שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the son did know his father's teaching. He holds that it does not apply to the עומר, because the fats-and-limbs case has a special feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of burning fats and limbs, the animal's שחיטה had already pushed aside שבת. So it makes sense to finish the job on time. The עומר has no earlier act that overrode שבת, so the only reason its reaping may override שבת is that it would be invalid at any other time.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces a new answer)
it is different there
slaughtering of the animal
overrode / pushed aside שבת

phrases.english: Rather, there it is different,
phrases.notes: "There" is the case of burning fats and limbs on שבת, which was the basis of רבי שמעון's teaching.

phrases.english: since the slaughtering already overrode Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by showing a difference between the two cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי שמעון's principle applies equally to the עומר, which would cancel the proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: The principle only applies where שבת was already overridden (by the שחיטה). The עומר has no such earlier step, so the proof stands.

steps.title: The same logic should apply to רבי
steps.stepSummary: If that distinction is right, רבי should agree that the עומר is invalid at the wrong time, yet he says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי too, the slaughtering overrode שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around against רבי. רבי holds that an עומר reaped at the wrong time is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי also must admit that in the fats-and-limbs case the שחיטה already overrode שבת. Then he too should conclude that the עומר's reaping overrides שבת only because it would be invalid otherwise. That contradicts his ruling that it is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)
here too / the same applies

steps.confusionAlert: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, a specific sage. It is not a general word for "a rabbi."

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi, here too
the slaughtering overrode Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי הָכִי נָמֵי דָּחֲתָה שְׁחִיטָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the distinction from step 2 to challenge רבי's opposing view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that an עומר reaped at the wrong time is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The step 2 distinction applies to everyone. So reaping overriding שבת should prove invalidity for רבי too.

steps.title: רבי holds that reaping the עומר does not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי avoids the problem because, in his view, the עומר is not reaped on שבת at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי holds that reaping the עומר does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of רבי. He does not accept the starting point that the reaping overrides שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof that a wrongly-timed עומר is invalid rested on reaping overriding שבת. רבי denies that reaping overrides שבת, so the proof never gets started. That is why he can say a wrongly-timed reaping is still valid.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds / his view is
reaping of the barley for the עומר offering
does not override

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi holds:
the reaping of the omer does not override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by rejecting its starting assumption for רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that reaping the עומר overrides שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי holds that reaping the עומר does not override שבת, so the proof of invalidity does not apply to him.

steps.title: A משנה seems to say the עומר is reaped even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה whose wording assumes the עומר is reaped on שבת, against what was just said about רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does it not override? But we learned: The חכמים say, both on שבת and on a weekday it came from three סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer with a משנה. That משנה talks about how much barley was reaped on שבת, which shows the reaping happened on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, רבי ישמעאל says the amount reaped on שבת was different from a weekday, and the חכמים say it was three סאה either way. Both sides assume reaping took place on שבת. So it seems everyone agrees reaping overrides שבת, which goes against what we said about רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: and the Sages (the majority view)
both on שבת and on a weekday
a regular weekday
from three (סאה of barley)

phrases.english: And does it not? But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה earlier in this מסכת (63b), where רבי ישמעאל gave a different amount reaped on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֶחָד שַׁבָּת וְאֶחָד חוֹל –
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: both on Shabbat and on a weekday
it would come from three.
phrases.notes: Three סאה of barley, a measure of volume.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 4's claim about רבי by quoting a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that reaping the עומר does not override שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה describes how much was reaped on שבת, so reaping on שבת must be allowed.

steps.title: That משנה does not follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה reflects other opinions, not רבי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: That משנה is not according to רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply. The משנה that assumes reaping on שבת does not follow רבי, so it does not disprove his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions in that משנה hold that reaping overrides שבת, but רבי is not one of them. So רבי can still hold that reaping does not override שבת. That lets him say a wrongly-timed reaping is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not in accordance with...

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that a wrongly-timed עומר is invalid, because reaping overrides שבת and nothing earlier overrode שבת. רבי holds the עומר is valid, because in his view reaping does not override שבת at all. The משנה that implies otherwise does not follow רבי.

phrases.english: That is not in accordance with Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by saying the quoted משנה does not reflect רבי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה reflects everyone's view, including רבי's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows other תנאים. רבי disagrees and holds that reaping does not override שבת.

steps.title: The Sages' opinion also assumes reaping on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the same משנה, who say the עומר is reaped on שבת and on weekdays alike, by three people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: on שבת and on a weekday alike, it is reaped by three people, with three baskets and three sickles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from a משנה that seems to assume the עומר is reaped on שבת. This again challenges the claim that רבי holds it is not reaped on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argue only about how many people reap on שבת. Both sides take for granted that reaping does happen on שבת. That clashes with what was said about רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular weekday
Baskets that hold the cut barley
Sickles used for reaping

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Both on Shabbat and on a weekday
it is by three people, with three baskets
and with three sickles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד שַׁבָּת וְאֶחָד חוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further challenge from the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 4 that רבי holds the עומר is not reaped on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the משנה assume that reaping on שבת happens, so the משנה seems to contradict what was said about רבי.

steps.title: That clause is not like רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this clause also follows other opinions, not רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not in line with רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: this part of the משנה does not follow רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to explain the משנה differently. Both the חכמים and רבי חנינא simply hold that the עומר is reaped on שבת, and רבי disagrees with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with רבי's opinion

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה reflects the view of רבי too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows opinions that disagree with רבי.

steps.title: The reaper asks 'this שבת?'
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה describes the reaper asking the crowd about reaping on this שבת, which assumes reaping on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on שבת he says to them: 'This שבת?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different משנה, where the reaper asks the people whether to reap on this שבת. That again assumes the עומר is reaped on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question makes sense only if reaping on שבת really takes place. So this משנה also seems to go against what was said about רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This שבת?', a question asked aloud before reaping

phrases.english: And on Shabbat he says to them:
phrases.notes: This is the court's messenger, who asks the people watching a set list of questions before he cuts the barley.

phrases.english: "On this Shabbat?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי holds the עומר is not reaped on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ceremony of asking 'this שבת?' assumes that reaping happens on שבת.

steps.title: This too is not like רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again answers that this משנה does not follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not in line with רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: Same answer once more: this משנה follows the opinions that disagree with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps its claim about רבי. It puts every source that assumes reaping on שבת into the camp of the other opinions.

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with Rabbi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion

steps.title: A משנה that must be רבי's says it overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the עומר reaped by day is valid and overrides שבת. Only רבי holds that reaping by day is valid, so this משנה must be his.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If it was reaped by day it is valid, and it overrides שבת.' Who holds that reaping by day is valid? רבי. And it teaches 'it overrides שבת.' Doesn't that mean the reaping?
steps.whatsHappening: This time the גמרא picks a משנה that cannot be pushed aside as 'not like רבי', because it clearly follows רבי. That משנה says the עומר overrides שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half, that reaping by day is valid, is רבי's view. So the second half, 'overrides שבת', should also be רבי's. That seems to show רבי holds the reaping is done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaped during the day, when it should be reaped at night
Valid
Overrides the prohibitions of שבת
'Doesn't it mean...?', used to suggest a reading
Reaping

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier the גמרא could answer 'not like רבי'. That answer doesn't work here, because the first half of this משנה is clearly רבי's view.

phrases.english: If it was reaped during the day, it is fit,
and it overrides Shabbat.
Whom have you heard who says:
If it was reaped during the day, it is fit?
Rabbi.
And it teaches: And it overrides Shabbat.
Is it not referring to reaping?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger challenge from a source that clearly follows רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי holds the עומר is not reaped on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה is רבי's, and it says the עומר overrides שבת, which suggests the reaping is done on שבת.

steps.title: It means the offering, not the reaping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'overrides שבת' means offering the עומר on the מזבח, not reaping it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means for the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה differently. What overrides שבת is bringing the עומר as an offering, not the reaping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By narrowing 'overrides שבת' to the offering, the גמרא keeps its claim that in רבי's view the reaping is not done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the offering on the מזבח

phrases.english: No, it is referring to the sacrifice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11.

steps.title: רבי's ברייתא about the מועדים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does reaping really not override שבת for רבי? It starts quoting a ברייתא where רבי learns from a פסוק about the festival offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But reaping does not override שבת? Isn't it taught: רבי says, 'And משה declared the appointed times of ה'.' Why does the פסוק say this? Because we had learned only about the תמיד and the פסח, where it says 'in its appointed time': 'in its appointed time', even on שבת; 'in its appointed time', even in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave by bringing a ברייתא of רבי. This step sets up the challenge, and the ברייתא continues in steps 14 and 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי starts from the rule that the תמיד and פסח override שבת and טומאה because the תורה says 'in its appointed time'. He then uses the פסוק of 'the appointed times of ה'' to extend this to the other festival offerings. That will suggest the עומר's needs, reaping included, also override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why does the פסוק need to say this?'
The daily offering
The Pesach offering
'In its appointed time', teaching that the offering must be brought at its set time no matter what
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: But with regard to reaping, it does not override Shabbat?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi says:
"And Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:44

phrases.english: Why does the verse state this?
Because we had learned only
about the daily offering and the Paschal offering,
phrases.notes: He means we only knew that these two override שבת and טומאה.

phrases.english: as it is stated concerning them: "In its appointed time":
phrases.notes: במדבר 9:2 and 28:2

phrases.english: "In its appointed time," even on Shabbat;
"In its appointed time," even in ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that for רבי only the offering of the עומר, not its reaping, overrides שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's ברייתא extends the 'appointed time' rule beyond the תמיד and פסח to the other festival offerings, which implies the עומר's reaping also overrides שבת.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: the other communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי continues: the rest of the קרבנות הציבור also override שבת, learned from the פסוק about offerings brought in their appointed times.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the rest of the communal offerings also override שבת? The פסוק says: 'These you shall offer to ה׳ in your appointed times.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it started in step 13. Here רבי extends the rule of overriding שבת to all the other קרבנות הציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'במועדיכם' (in your appointed times) teaches that these offerings must be brought at their set time, even on שבת. This builds up the list of offerings that override שבת, and the ברייתא keeps expanding it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings, brought on behalf of all of כלל ישראל
The פסוק teaches (introduces the source of a derivation)
In your appointed times: the offering has a fixed time that cannot be pushed off

phrases.english: The rest of the communal offerings, from where do we know?
The verse teaches:
"These you shall offer to the Lord in your appointed times."
phrases.notes: במדבר 29:39

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 13 as the basis of the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All communal offerings override שבת, learned from 'במועדיכם'.

steps.title: The ברייתא includes the עומר and the שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds the עומר and the שתי הלחם, along with the offerings brought with each, from the פסוק 'וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we include the עומר and the offerings brought with it, and the שתי הלחם and the offerings brought with them? The פסוק says: 'And משה declared the appointed times of ה׳.' The פסוק set one appointed time for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now includes the עומר and the שתי הלחם in the rule. Like the other communal offerings, they also override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מועדי ה׳' covers all the times listed in that פרשה, so everything brought at those times has a fixed time that pushes aside שבת. This is the key line. The גמרא will now ask what exactly 'overriding שבת' means for the עומר and the שתי הלחם.

keyTerms.meaning: To include something extra in the rule
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The animal offerings brought together with it
Set a fixed appointed time

phrases.english: From where do we include the omer, and what is offered with it?
phrases.notes: With the עומר a lamb is brought as a עולה.

phrases.english: The two loaves, and what is offered with them?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת מֹעֲדֵי ה׳״ –
phrases.english: The verse teaches: "And Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:44

phrases.english: The verse set a fixed time for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by adding the עומר and the שתי הלחם to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the offerings brought with them all override שבת.

steps.title: What part of these offerings overrides שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what overriding שבת means here. It cannot mean offering on the מזבח, because the שתי הלחם are never offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what does it override שבת? If you say for offering it, are the שתי הלחם something that gets offered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops quoting and asks what the ברייתא meant. It rules out one possible reading and sets up the real point in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the גמרא said that 'overrides שבת' means offering on the מזבח. That reading cannot work here, because the שתי הלחם are not burned on the מזבח at all. So the ברייתא must be talking about some other kind of work.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? (asking what something refers to)
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Offering on the מזבח
Things that get offered on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is asking whether the עומר is offered on the מזבח. The question is about the שתי הלחם, which are waved and eaten by כהנים but never put on the מזבח.

phrases.english: For what?
phrases.notes: For what does the ברייתא say these override שבת?

phrases.english: If you say for offering it,
are the two loaves something that gets offered?
phrases.notes: No. The שתי הלחם never go on the מזבח, so offering them can't be what overrides שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא just quoted and rules out reading it as 'offering on the מזבח'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which act does the ברייתא mean when it says the עומר and the שתי הלחם override שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It cannot mean offering, since the שתי הלחם are not offered. The answer comes in step 17.

steps.title: So for רבי, reaping the עומר overrides שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean the preparation work: grinding and sifting for the שתי הלחם, and reaping for the עומר. So for רבי, reaping the עומר overrides שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means grinding and sifting. In the same way, for the עומר it means reaping, and that overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion: in רבי's ברייתא, the preparation work overrides שבת. That includes reaping the עומר, which completes the challenge that began in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שתי הלחם are not offered, their overriding שבת must refer to grinding and sifting the flour. The parallel for the עומר is reaping. This contradicts the claim from step 4, defended in step 12, that for רבי reaping does not override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Grinding the grain
Sifting the flour
Similar to it; the parallel case
Reaping the grain
Overrides שבת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ברייתא shows that the preparation of the עומר and the שתי הלחם overrides שבת. So for רבי, reaping the עומר overrides שבת, which goes against the answers given earlier.
steps.whyThisMatters: This undoes the earlier answers that tried to separate רבי from reaping on שבת. The גמרא will now need a new way to read this ברייתא of רבי.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: for grinding and sifting,
and similarly, regarding the omer, for reaping,
and it overrides Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Since this ברייתא is רבי's, reaping overrides שבת according to רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 and uses that answer to finish the challenge opened in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 4, defended in step 12) that according to רבי reaping the עומר does not override שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is רבי's. The שתי הלחם are not offered, so overriding שבת must mean preparation work. The parallel for the עומר is reaping, so reaping overrides שבת for רבי.

steps.title: A new reading: the עומר for offering, the loaves for baking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא differently. The עומר overrides שבת only for its offering. The שתי הלחם override שבת for baking, because רבי holds that the oven makes them holy. If they were baked on Friday, they would become פסול by being left overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא means the עומר overrides שבת for its offering, and the שתי הלחם override שבת for their baking. רבי holds that the oven makes things holy, so if one baked the loaves the day before, they would become פסול by being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the reading from step 17. It now explains the ברייתא in a way that does not say reaping overrides שבת for רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the גמרא read the ברייתא as talking about preparation work, like reaping the עומר. Now it says the two items are not parallel: for the עומר only the offering itself overrides שבת. For the שתי הלחם, the baking overrides שבת, because the oven makes them holy, and holy loaves baked a day early would be ruined by staying overnight.

keyTerms.meaning: Offering a קרבן on the מזבח
Baking
The oven makes holy: a baked offering becomes holy once it is baked in the oven
Being left overnight, which makes holy items פסול

steps.confusionAlert: Baking the loaves on Friday is not a problem in itself. The problem only comes because רבי supposedly holds the oven makes them holy, and holy loaves become פסול if left overnight.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading saves the earlier idea that reaping does not override שבת for רבי. But it depends on רבי holding תנור מקדש, and the גמרא attacks exactly that point next.

phrases.english: Rather, the omer is for its offering,
and the two loaves are for baking,
and Rabbi holds the oven consecrates,
so if he bakes it from yesterday,
it becomes disqualified by being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the step 17 reading of the ברייתא and offers a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the two items in the ברייתא override שבת in different ways
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means preparation work, so reaping the עומר overrides שבת for רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עומר overrides שבת only for its offering. The loaves override שבת for baking, because the oven makes them holy and they would be ruined overnight.

steps.title: Challenge: the loaves become holy through the lambs' slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי really holds that the oven makes the loaves holy. A ברייתא teaches that the שבועות lambs make the loaves holy only through their slaughter, for their proper purpose (לשמן).
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי really hold that the oven makes things holy? But a ברייתא teaches: the lambs of עצרת make the loaves holy only through their slaughter. How? If he slaughtered them for their own purpose and sprinkled their blood for their own purpose, the loaves become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the key idea behind step 18. It brings a ברייתא showing that something else makes the loaves holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loaves only become holy when the lambs are slaughtered, the oven does not make them holy. Then baking them on Friday would not ruin them by לינה. So there would be no reason for baking to override שבת, and the reading from step 18 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The two lambs brought as שלמים with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
Slaughtering the animal
For their own purpose: done with the correct intent for this specific קרבן
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: And does Rabbi hold that the oven consecrates?
But it is taught: the lambs of Atzeret
phrases.notes: עצרת is another name for שבועות.

phrases.english: do not consecrate the bread
except through slaughter. How so?
If he slaughtered them for their sake,
and sprinkled their blood for their sake, the bread is consecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 18 that רבי holds תנור מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that רבי holds the oven makes the loaves holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the loaves become holy only through the lambs' slaughter. So the oven does not make them holy, and Friday baking would not cause לינה problems.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: improper intent at slaughter or sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: If both the slaughter and the sprinkling were not for their proper purpose, the loaves are not holy. If the slaughter was proper but the sprinkling was not, the loaves are 'holy and not holy.' These are the words of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered them not for their own purpose and sprinkled their blood not for their own purpose, the bread is not holy. If he slaughtered them for their own purpose but sprinkled their blood not for their own purpose, the bread is holy and not holy. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with more cases. Its last words show that this whole teaching is רבי's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'holy and not holy' case shows that for רבי the slaughter is what starts the loaves' holiness. A proper slaughter alone already gives them some holiness. Since the ruling is labeled דברי רבי, it is a direct source against saying רבי holds the oven makes the loaves holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for their own purpose: done with the wrong intent
Partly holy: holy enough that it cannot be redeemed, but not holy enough to be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: 'דברי רבי' at the end refers to the whole ברייתא, starting from step 19. That is why it works as a challenge against רבי.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered them not for their sake,
and sprinkled their blood not for their sake,
the bread is not consecrated.
If he slaughtered them for their sake,
and sprinkled their blood not for their sake,
the bread is consecrated and not consecrated,
phrases.notes: Holy enough that it can't be redeemed, but not holy enough to be eaten.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 19 and names רבי as its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי, the slaughter of the lambs is what makes the loaves holy. A proper slaughter with improper sprinkling leaves them partly holy.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: both steps must be proper
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees with רבי. He says the loaves are never holy unless both the slaughter and the sprinkling are done for their proper purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: the bread is never holy until he slaughters the lambs for their own purpose and sprinkles their blood for their own purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a different opinion. It argues with רבי's middle case, where only the slaughter was proper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does not accept partial holiness from the slaughter alone. He requires the sprinkling too. Both opinions agree that the lambs' קרבן, not the oven, makes the loaves holy. So the challenge against רבי from step 19 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: never, in any case

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, רבי holds that the slaughter of the שבועות lambs makes the שתי הלחם holy. That contradicts the claim in step 18 that רבי holds תנור מקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
it is never consecrated,
until he slaughters them for their sake
and sprinkles their blood for their sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא, arguing with רבי's middle case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves become holy only if both the slaughter and the blood sprinkling are done for their proper purpose.

steps.title: Holy means fixed, not first made holy
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'holy and not holy' in רבי's ברייתא means 'fixed and not fixed.' So רבי can still hold that the oven makes the loaves holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: When רבי says 'holy' and 'not holy,' he means the loaves are 'fixed' or 'not fixed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19. רבי's words about the lambs making the loaves holy are about the loaves becoming 'fixed,' not about when they first become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oven is what first makes the שתי הלחם holy. The proper slaughter and sprinkling of the lambs only 'fix' the loaves, so they are locked in as the שבועות loaves and can no longer be switched to another use. So there is no contradiction, and the answer in Step 18 stands: the baking overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They became fixed, locked in for their special purpose
They did not become fixed, so they can still be switched
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The oven makes the loaves holy

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, the oven makes the שתי הלחם holy. The lambs only 'fix' the loaves for שבועות. That is why their baking must be done on the day itself, even on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Holy' in רבי's ברייתא does not mean 'becoming holy for the first time.' Here it means 'becoming fixed' for this one purpose.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
He is saying 'fixed' and 'not fixed.'
phrases.notes: רבי's words 'holy and not holy' in Step 20 really mean the loaves are locked in, or not locked in, as the שבועות loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק הוּקְבְּעוּ וְלֹא הוּקְבְּעוּ קָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 19-21 by reading רבי's words in the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of terms: 'holy' means 'fixed' for its purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי holds that the loaves become holy only through the slaughter of the lambs, not through the oven.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oven makes the loaves holy. The lambs only fix them as the שבועות loaves, so רבי's view in Step 18 stands.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק called רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is over, and the גמרא says its traditional goodbye line. Nothing new is being argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן marks the end of a פרק and shows love for the learning, with the hope of coming back to it. The next line starts a brand new משנה and topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula at the end of a פרק
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא

phrases.english: We will return to you, Rabbi Yishmael.
phrases.notes: 'רבי ישמעאל' here is the name of the פרק, taken from its opening words, not someone being spoken to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק after the last question was answered in Step 22.

steps.title: List of מנחות that have a handful removed
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the מנחות from which a קומץ is removed, with the rest eaten by the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the מנחות from which a handful is taken, and the rest goes to the כהנים: the fine flour offering, the pan offering, the deep-pan offering, the oven loaves, the oven wafers, the מנחה of non-Jews, the מנחה of women, the עומר, the sinner's מנחה, and the מנחת קנאות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It lists the kinds of מנחות whose procedure is: take a קומץ for the מזבח, and give the rest to the כהנים to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list mixes private offerings (fine flour, pan, deep pan, loaves, wafers), offerings from special people (non-Jews, women), a public offering (the עומר), and offerings for specific situations (the sinner's מנחה and the סוטה's מנחת קנאות). They all share the same basic rule: a קומץ goes on the מזבח, and the שיריים go to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A קומץ, a handful, is taken from them for the מזבח
The leftover part of the מנחה after the קומץ is removed
A flat pan, used for a fried מנחה
A deep pan, used for a מנחה cooked in more oil
A poor sinner's flour offering, brought in place of an animal
The barley offering brought by a סוטה

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the meal offerings from which a handful is removed,
and their remainder goes to the priests:
the fine flour offering, and the pan offering, and the deep-pan offering,
and the loaves, and the wafers,
the offering of non-Jews, and the offering of women,
and the omer offering, and the sinner's offering,
and the offering of jealousy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק and topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These ten kinds of מנחות have a קומץ removed for the מזבח, and their remainder is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: A כהן's sinner offering is split in two
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that a כהן's מנחת חוטא also has a קומץ removed. The קומץ and the rest are each burned on the מזבח separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: A sinner's מנחה brought by a כהן has a handful removed. The handful is offered by itself, and the rest is offered by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a special case to the list: a כהן who brings a sinner's מנחה. A קומץ is taken from it too, but the rest is not eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's מנחה is normally burned whole and never eaten (ויקרא 6:16). רבי שמעון says that a כהן's מנחת חוטא still has a קומץ removed, like any other sinner's מנחה. Since a כהן's מנחה cannot be eaten, the rest is also burned on the מזבח, but separately from the קומץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
It is offered by itself, separately
A מנחה brought by a כהן, normally burned whole and never eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the כהנים eat the rest here. In this case the rest is also burned on the מזבח, just separately from the קומץ.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
the sinner's offering of priests has a handful removed,
and the handful is offered by itself,
and the remainder is offered by itself.
phrases.notes: 'Offered' means burned on the מזבח, since a כהן's מנחה is never eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים נִקְמֶצֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special case to the משנה's list: a כהן's sinner offering, where the remainder is not eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן's מנחת חוטא has a קומץ removed. The קומץ and the remainder are each burned on the מזבח separately.

steps.title: רב פפא: The Baked Offerings Always Come as Ten
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states that wherever the משנה mentions the baked מנחות, it means a set of ten items.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: רב פפא said: Every place where we learned in the משנה about these baked offerings, we learned that there are ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the new משנה with a rule from רב פפא. Whenever the משנה mentions the baked מנחות, it means ten items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed baked מנחות, like מאפה תנור, without giving a number. רב פפא fills that in: these always come as ten pieces. The next steps ask what this rule is coming to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים that explains the משנה
Ten, the number of loaves or wafers in these מנחות

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Pappa said:
Every place where we learned [these offerings]
we learned ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דִּתְנַן – עֶשֶׂר תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baked מנחות in the משנה always come as ten items.

steps.title: What Is רב פפא Teaching Us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point רב פפא's rule adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this. It is setting up the next step, which explains his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That these מנחות come as ten seems already known. So the גמרא looks for the real point behind רב פפא's words.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asked when a statement seems obvious)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what new point step 26 adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea רב פפא's rule of ten teaches.

steps.title: It Excludes רבי שמעון's Half-and-Half View
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא comes to reject רבי שמעון, who allows five חלות and five רקיקין. All ten must be of one type.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי שמעון, who said one may bring half loaves and half wafers. He teaches us that one may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא is ruling against רבי שמעון. The ten must all be the same kind, not a mix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real point is not the number ten but the type. רבי שמעון lets a person split the ten into loaves and wafers. רב פפא teaches that our משנה holds all ten must be one kind.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning to reject another opinion
Thick loaves
Thin wafers
Half

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב פפא is arguing about the number ten. Everyone agrees on ten. The argument is only whether you may mix loaves and wafers.

phrases.english: To exclude [the view] of Rabbi Shimon,
who said:
he may bring half loaves and half wafers;
he teaches us that [he may] not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא rejects רבי שמעון's half-and-half view. All ten must be one type.
steps.whatToRemember: The ten baked items of a מנחה must all be חלות or all רקיקין. Unlike רבי שמעון, you can't mix them.

steps.title: Source That the כהנים Eat the Leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and their remainder goes to the כהנים' and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'And their remainder goes to the כהנים.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה. It asks where we learn that the כהנים eat what is left after the קומץ is taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24's משנה said the שירים of these מנחות are eaten by the כהנים. Now the גמרא wants the פסוק behind that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover part of the מנחה after the קומץ is removed
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: "And their remainder goes to the priests":
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new phrase of the משנה from step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the כהנים eat the שירים of the מנחות.

steps.title: Why Ask? The Torah Already Says It
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own question. Some מנחות say it outright, and a general פסוק covers the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where it is written, it is written. Where it is not written, the פסוק says about it: 'And this is the law of the מנחה: the sons of אהרן shall offer it... and what remains of it, אהרן and his sons shall eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question. The answer seems obvious: for some מנחות the תורה says it directly, and a general פסוק in ויקרא covers all the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There seems to be no need to search for a source. For some מנחות the תורה states the rule outright. 'This is the law of the מנחה' is a general rule for every מנחה that the כהנים eat the leftovers.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the מנחה, a general rule for all מנחות
What remains, the leftover part

phrases.english: That which is written is written,
phrases.notes: For some מנחות the תורה already says the כהנים eat the leftovers.

phrases.english: and that which is not written,
it is written regarding it:
"And this is the law of the meal offering:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7–9

phrases.english: the sons of Aaron shall offer it, etc.
And the remainder of it
Aaron and his sons shall eat."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיבָא – כְּתִיבָא, וּדְלָא כְּתִיבָא – כְּתִיב בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question in step 29.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is obvious. The תורה states it for some מנחות, and 'תורת המנחה' covers all the others.

steps.title: The Real Question Was About Barley Offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that it never asked about wheat מנחות. It asked about מנחות that come from barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a מנחה that comes from wheat we had no question. Our question was about a מנחה that comes from barley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its question by narrowing it. The general פסוק covers wheat מנחות, but the question is about barley ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most מנחות are wheat, so 'תורת המנחה' clearly covers them. Barley מנחות are a different kind, so maybe the general פסוק does not include them. That is why the גמרא still needs a source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat
Barley
We had no question about this

phrases.english: [A meal offering] that comes from wheat:
we had no question;
where we had a question
was [one] that comes from barley.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאָה חִיטִּין – לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לַן, כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן – בָּאָה שְׂעוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30's challenge by narrowing the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about all מנחות, so the general פסוק answers it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was only about barley מנחות, which the general פסוק may not cover.

steps.title: Barley Too: A קומץ Means the Rest Goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: barley מנחות have a קומץ removed, so their leftovers must go to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Barley מנחות too: since a קומץ is taken from them, their leftovers go to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again: even for barley there should be no question. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will narrow its question once more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking a קומץ only makes sense if the rest is set aside for the כהנים to eat. Barley מנחות also have a קומץ, so the same logic should apply. The question seems to fall away again.

keyTerms.meaning: A קומץ (handful) is removed from it

phrases.english: [One] that comes from barley also:
since a handful is removed from it,
its remainder goes to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאָה שְׂעוֹרִין נָמֵי, מִדְּנִקְמֶצֶת – שְׁיָרֶיהָ לַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed question of step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 31 that barley מנחות need their own source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing a קומץ shows the rest belongs to the כהנים, and barley מנחות have a קומץ too.

steps.title: The question was only according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 32. According to the רבנן, taking a קומץ does prove the rest is eaten. But רבי שמעון holds there is a מנחה that has a קומץ taken and is still not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, we had no question. Our question is according to רבי שמעון, who says there is a מנחה that has a קומץ removed and is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its question. It explains that the question only works according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 argued: if a קומץ is taken, the leftovers automatically go to the כהנים. That is true for the רבנן. But רבי שמעון knows of a case where a קומץ is taken and the rest is not eaten, so for him the קומץ proves nothing, and we still need a source.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of...
That has a קומץ (handful) removed
And is not eaten

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן;
phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, we have no question;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן – אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: when we do have a question – it is according to Rabbi Shimon,
who says: there is a meal offering
that has a handful removed but is not eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 by limiting the question to רבי שמעון's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the question to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Taking a קומץ always proves the leftovers are eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, a קומץ does not prove the leftovers are eaten, so a source is still needed.

steps.title: The משנה showing רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where רבי שמעון says a כהן's מנחת חוטא has a קומץ taken, but both the קומץ and the leftovers go on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי שמעון says: the sin-offering מנחה of כהנים has a קומץ removed. The קומץ is offered by itself, and the leftovers are offered by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי שמעון really holds that a מנחה can have a קומץ taken and still not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the leftovers are burned on the מזבח, not eaten by the כהנים. So for רבי שמעון, taking a קומץ does not automatically mean the rest is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: The מנחה brought by a sinner
Has a קומץ (handful) removed
The leftovers of the מנחה after the קומץ is taken

phrases.english: As we learned in the Mishna: Rabbi Shimon says:
the sinner's meal offering of priests has a handful removed,
the handful is offered by itself,
and the remainder is offered by itself.
phrases.notes: "Offered" means burned on the מזבח, so nobody eats these leftovers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim about רבי שמעון made in step 33.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a מנחה can have a קומץ taken and not be eaten.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the מנחת חוטא of כהנים.

steps.title: So where do we learn it?
steps.stepSummary: With the question now properly framed, the גמרא asks again: according to רבי שמעון, where do we learn that barley מנחות are eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question, now that it has shown why the question is real. This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ argument from step 32 cannot work for רבי שמעון. So the גמרא needs a real source that the כהנים eat the leftovers of barley מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we learn that the כהנים eat the leftovers of barley מנחות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the original question of steps 29 and 31 after defending it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the leftovers of barley מנחות go to the כהנים, according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: חזקיה's source: an extra פסוק applied to barley
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה quotes the פסוק 'every מנחה mixed with oil or dry shall belong to all the sons of אהרן'. Wheat מנחות are already covered elsewhere, so this פסוק is applied to barley מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: the פסוק says 'And every מנחה, mixed with oil or dry, shall belong to all the sons of אהרן.' If it is not needed for a mixed wheat מנחה, apply it to a mixed barley מנחה. If it is not needed for a dry wheat מנחה, apply it to a dry barley מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question with a פסוק. Since that פסוק is not needed for wheat מנחות, he uses it for barley מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from other sources that the leftovers of wheat מנחות go to the כהנים, so this פסוק would be extra for them. So we apply it to barley: the mixed barley מנחה is the עומר, and the dry barley מנחה is the מנחת סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed with oil
Dry, without oil
If it is not needed for this case, apply it to another case
Barley
Wheat

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה's source, according to רבי שמעון, that the כהנים eat the leftovers of barley מנחות is an extra פסוק (ויקרא 7:10), applied to barley because wheat is already covered. The next step challenges this source.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said: As the verse states:
"And every meal offering, mixed with oil, or dry,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

phrases.english: shall all the sons of Aaron have."

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לִבְלוּלָה שֶׁל חִיטִּין –
phrases.english: If it is not needed for a mixed meal offering of wheat –
apply it to a mixed meal offering of barley,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לַחֲרֵבָה שֶׁל חִיטִּין –
phrases.english: and if it is not needed for a dry meal offering of wheat –
apply it to a dry meal offering of barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 7:10 is extra for wheat מנחות, so it teaches that the leftovers of barley מנחות, both mixed and dry, go to the כהנים.

steps.title: Isn't this פסוק needed for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges חזקיה: the same פסוק is needed for a ברייתא's teaching that כהנים may not trade shares of מנחות for shares of animal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this פסוק really come to teach this? Isn't it needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: from where do we know that one does not divide מנחות against animal offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks חזקיה's answer. It says the פסוק is not extra, because it already teaches a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה's whole argument depends on the פסוק being extra for wheat מנחות. If the פסוק is busy teaching that מנחות cannot be traded for animal offerings, then it is not free to teach about barley. The ברייתא continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this really come to teach this?
But it is needed for something else
Divide shares among the כהנים
In exchange for animal offerings

phrases.english: And does this verse come for this purpose?
Isn't it needed for that which is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין חוֹלְקִין מְנָחוֹת כְּנֶגֶד זְבָחִים –
phrases.english: From where is it derived that priests may not take shares of meal offerings in exchange for animal offerings –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא? הָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges חזקיה's source from step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's use of ויקרא 7:10 for barley מנחות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is not extra, because a ברייתא uses it to teach that מנחות may not be traded for shares of animal offerings.
